canonicalNote: This is the authoritative snapshot: the firmware version is known and the capture is natively pristine. Prefer it over 2026-03-01_firmware-unknown for any argument about the format, and use it as the golden-file fixture source when the test suite is created.
capturedByNote: tools/Get-DeviceTemplateCorpus.ps1 failed on first use and was not debugged; the manual path was quicker. The script's firmware-detection bug was fixed using the device output recorded below, but the script itself remains unexercised end-to-end.
firmwareVersionNote: IMG_VERSION is the reMarkable release version. VERSION_ID on this device is 6.0.112, which is the underlying Codex Linux (OpenEmbedded) build and NOT the firmware -- using it would label this snapshot plausibly and wrongly. /usr/share/remarkable/update.conf does not exist on this firmware. The distro name 'Codex Linux' is reMarkable's OpenEmbedded build and is unrelated to the Codex CLI used as a reviewer in ADR-0009.

provenance.note: Taken straight off the device after the update and reboot, before the owner re-applied his custom templates. The capture is therefore natively pristine -- 65 stock templates and a manifest with no user entries -- requiring no cleanup to be comparable. This is what makes it better evidence than the March capture, whose manifest was restored from a saved-aside copy.

integrity.aggregateScope: sha256 of the concatenated per-file sha256 digests of stock/*.template plus templates.json, filenames sorted; truncated to 32 hex chars
integrity.perFileHashesOmitted: Git content-hashes every file, so per-file digests here would duplicate that with no benefit. The aggregate exists because it is a single value comparable across snapshots.

contents.stock/: The 65 templates reMarkable ships on this firmware. All declare "author": "reMarkable".
contents.templates.json: The stock manifest exactly as the firmware left it. 79 entries for 65 files: a filename may appear twice, once per orientation.

userTemplatesNote: The owner's custom templates are deliberately NOT in this snapshot. They are not firmware artefacts, so they live in research/reference_material/user_templates/ instead of being duplicated into every snapshot.
